steps.title: Reading the danger boxplot
steps.answers: What do the five boxes show about danger and sleep?
steps.opens: What is wrong with a bar of means, and how do you fix it?
steps.statement: Across danger levels 1 to 5 the boxes sit lower: mammals at high risk of predation sleep less, and the spread inside each level is wide.

explain.text: Compare the thick median lines from left to right: they fall as danger rises. Compare the boxes too: they overlap, so danger is not the whole story; body size (sheet 04, scatterplot) and diet also matter. A boxplot suggests the pattern; the test of sheet 06 (several groups, so ANOVA or a rank test) says whether it is larger than chance.

terms.meaning: danger of predation, an index from 1 (low) to 5 (high)

steps.intuition: An animal that might be eaten cannot afford long, deep sleep.
steps.misconception: Falling medians prove that danger reduces sleep.

misconceptionFigure.caption: A pattern, not yet a cause.

wrong.title: Mistaken
wrong.text: Medians fall → danger causes short sleep.

right.title: Instead
right.text: Medians fall → test it, and think of body size.

check.q: Which test from sheet 06 compares sleep across the five danger levels?
check.a: ANOVA, summary(aov(TotalSleep ~ factor(Danger))), or a rank test if the boxes are skewed.
